title: Jeep Wrangler Engines by Year (1987–2026)
description: Every factory engine in the Jeep Wrangler by year, 1987–2026: the 2.5 four and 4.0 six, the 3.6 Pentastar, 2.0 turbo, EcoDiesel and the 392 V8.
intro: The Wrangler replaced the CJ for 1987 and has been built in four generations: the YJ, TJ, JK and JL. There was no 1996 model year; the YJ ended with 1995 and the TJ arrived as a 1997 model.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.

generations.name: YJ
intro: The YJ used AMC's 2.5 four and, through 1990, the carbureted 4.2 six. The fuel-injected 4.0 six replaced the 4.2 for 1991.

generations.name: TJ
intro: The coil-sprung TJ kept the 2.5 four and the 4.0 six; the 2.4 PowerTech four replaced the 2.5 for 2003. The Rubicon arrived in 2003 and the long-wheelbase Unlimited in 2004.

generations.name: JK
intro: The JK started with the 3.8 V6 and switched to the 3.6 Pentastar V6 for 2012. The JK was sold alongside the new JL during 2018.

generations.name: JL
intro: The JL offers the 3.6 Pentastar and a 2.0 turbo four, with the 3.0 EcoDiesel from 2020 to 2023, the 4xe plug-in hybrid from 2021 to 2025, and the 6.4 V8 of the 392 models from 2021.
